title: Slow downstream dependency
story: Every request waits 1.1 s on an external API. CPU is idle; more replicas cannot help. Expected: escalate.

timeline.thought:
Diagnosis complete — no resource change applies here.

Evidence review:
- Probe latency is consistently ~1103 ms (p50 1102.9, max 1105.3, last 5 samples 1105/1103/1103/1102/1103 ms), well over the 800 ms threshold and not recovering toward 500 ms.
- But CPU usage is `cpu_pct_avg_total: 0.0`, `cpu_pct_peak_total: 0.0` against a limit of 50% per replica — the container is essentially idle, not CPU-starved.
- Memory is `19.2 MiB` used out of a `128 MiB` limit (15%) — nowhere near OOM, no `oom_killed`, no restarts, exit_code 0.
- No errors in probe (`errors_recent: 0`), no crash-loop, single healthy replica, log shows a normal "listening" line.
- The service's documented purpose: "Search API; queries a third-party catalog service." Flat, uniform ~1.1s latency with zero CPU/memory pressure is the signature of a slow upstream dependency call (e.g., the catalog service), not local resource saturation.

Since latency isn't correlated with CPU or memory pressure at all, adding replicas or raising cpus/memory would not reduce per-request latency — it would just leave more idle containers waiting on the same slow dependency. This falls outside the "CPU saturation" and "OOM" fix patterns in watchdock.md, and the only allowed action here is `scale`, which won't touch the actual bottleneck (external call latency). Per the runbook, this needs escalation rather than a guardrail-bound resource change.

The single replica is idle, not resource-constrained, so this isn't CPU saturation or memory pressure. The service's own docs state it queries a third-party catalog service; flat elevated latency with zero CPU/memory load is consistent with a slow upstream dependency, which scaling replicas or raising cpus/memory (the only guardrail-allowed actions: 'scale') cannot fix. Needs human investigation of the catalog dependency/network path.
